bug_report_content:
id: 773
status: Fixed
summary: Switched order of "delete key" and "key in" statements changes semantic
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 0
commentCount: 5
Comment 0 (2012-07-09): // Input: var customData = { key: 'value' }; function testRemoveKey( key ) { var dataSlot = customData, retval = dataSlot && dataSlot[ key ], hadKey = dataSlot && ( key in dataSlot ); if ( dataSlot ) delete dataSlot[ key ]; return hadKey ? retval : null; }; console.log( testRemoveKey( 'key' ) ); // 'value' console.log( 'key' in customData ); // false // Compiled version: var customData={key:"value"};function testRemoveKey(b){var a=customData,c=a&&a[b];a&&delete a[b];return a&&b in a?c:null}console.log(testRemoveKey("key"));console.log("key"in customData); // null // false "b in a" is executed after "delete a[b]" what obviously doesn't make sense in this case. Reproducible on: http://closure-compiler.appspot.com/home and in "Version: 20120430 (revision 1918) Built on: 2012/04/30 18:02"
Comment 1 (2012-07-09): ack. thanks for the report
Comment 2 (2012-07-09): john figured this out first.
Comment 3 (2012-07-10): This issue was closed by revision r2079.
Comment 4 (2012-07-16): Thanks for quick patch :).
